displayQuote: Nothing in this world can take the place of persistence. Talent will not; nothing is more common than unsuccessful men with talent. Genius will not; unrewarded genius is almost a proverb. Education will not; the world is full of educated derelicts. Persistence and determination alone are omnipotent

schema.claimReviewed: Calvin Coolidge originated this exact persistence passage.
schema.claimQuoteText: Nothing in this world can take the place of persistence. Talent will not; nothing is more common than unsuccessful men with talent. Genius will not; unrewarded genius is almost a proverb. Education will not; the world is full of educated derelicts. Persistence and determination alone are omnipotent
schema.verdictNote: The displayed passage evolved across versions. Munger’s 1881 purpose passage is a precursor, Hart used a persistence version in 1902, and a later version was credited to Coolidge by 1929; the entire displayed wording is not a verbatim Munger quotation.
schema.faqAnswer: This passage is not original to Coolidge. Quote Investigator traces an evolving family through Munger’s 1881 purpose passage and Hart’s 1902 persistence version. The whole displayed wording should not be credited verbatim to Munger either.
